reason: The text explicitly portrays the Israelite people as victims of Egyptian oppression whose cries God has heard and whose suffering God acknowledges ('I have seen the affliction of my people which is in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters'). The narrative presents the Egyptian oppressors negatively and positions God as intervening to liberate the wronged people, not to punish them for wrongdoing. The people are depicted sympathetically as the afflicted party deserving deliverance, while Pharaoh and the Egyptian taskmasters are portrayed as oppressors. This contradicts the statement, which inverts the actual moral positioning of the text.
